mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the Solanaceae family is a common misconception?

options.A: Members typically have five fused petals forming a bell-shaped corolla.
options.B: Their fruits are always dry capsules.
options.C: Leaves are usually alternate and simple.
options.D: Many members contain alkaloids that can be toxic.

mcqs.answer: Their fruits are always dry capsules.
mcqs.explanation: Solanaceae fruits are characteristically berries (e.g., tomato, eggplant, pepper). While a few genera may produce capsule‑like fruits, the statement that all Solanaceae bear dry capsules is false and is a frequent misconception. Options A, C and D correctly describe typical Solanaceae features, making B the only incorrect statement.

mcqs.question: A flowering plant shows large, showy tepals arranged in two whorls of three, six stamens, and a superior ovary. Based on these characters, to which family does the plant most likely belong?
mcqs.explanation: Liliaceae are distinguished by flowers having six tepals (often appearing as petals) in two whorls, six stamens, and a superior ovary. Solanaceae have five fused petals, Fabaceae have a papilionaceous (zygomorphic) corolla, and Asteraceae possess composite heads. Hence the described features point to Liliaceae.

mcqs.question: Which set correctly matches each of the three families with its diagnostic floral character?

options.A: Fabaceae – zygomorphic (papilionaceous) corolla; Solanaceae – actinomorphic corolla with fused petals; Liliaceae – flowers with six tepals in two whorls.
options.B: Fabaceae – actinomorphic corolla with fused petals; Solanaceae – zygomorphic corolla; Liliaceae – flowers with four tepals.
options.C: Fabaceae – papilionaceous corolla; Solanaceae – flowers with separate petals; Liliaceae – flowers with fused petals.
options.D: Fabaceae – compound leaves; Solanaceae – opposite leaves; Liliaceae – whorled leaves.

mcqs.answer: Fabaceae – zygomorphic (papilionaceous) corolla; Solanaceae – actinomorphic corolla with fused petals; Liliaceae – flowers with six tepals in two whorls.
mcqs.explanation: Fabaceae (especially the subfamily Papilionoideae) have a distinctive bilaterally symmetric, papilionaceous corolla. Solanaceae flowers are radially symmetric (actinomorphic) with five fused petals forming a tubular corolla. Liliaceae are characterised by six tepals (often indistinguishable as petals) arranged in two whorls. Options B, C and D either misstate the floral symmetry or describe vegetative traits, not diagnostic floral characters.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a plant from the listed families with its major economic use?

options.A: Fabaceae – Soybean (source of protein‑rich oil and meal)

mcqs.answer: Fabaceae – Soybean (source of protein‑rich oil and meal)
mcqs.explanation: Soybean belongs to the Fabaceae family and is a key source of edible oil and protein meal worldwide. Wheat is a Poaceae member, not Solanaceae. Cotton belongs to Malvaceae, not Liliaceae. Rice is also a Poaceae member, not Fabaceae. Therefore only option A correctly links a family with an economically important species.
